epistemic_assessments.rationale: raf-tor-v3 is in force from 2025-01-15 and states second-line challenge to first-line risk acceptance.
The 2026-02-18 minutes record the Forum rejecting the delivery team's 'representative coverage' position and attaching a condition.
Acceptance granted subject to a coverage improvement plan and a 90-day review.
The Ashcombe risk pack duplicates the design authority pack's data flows, retention position, model performance and cohort breakdown.
The Forum accepts risk; whether it may direct or halt the change itself is not addressed.

epistemic_assessments.scope_searched: raf-tor-v3 in full; RAF minutes 2026-02; efficiency review 2026-01.

epistemic_assessments.rationale: raf-tor-v3 confers second-line challenge on the Forum and was in force at the relevant time.
raf-tor-v3 states the Forum may refuse an acceptance, with refusal escalating to Board Risk Committee.
No source addresses containment of an accepted risk that subsequently deteriorates.

epistemic_assessments.rationale: Refusal power escalating past the accepting function, a second-line reporting line and one evidenced rejection of a first-line position support partial independence; four members shared with the design authority and packs prepared by the delivery team qualify it.

stated_purpose: Provide second-line challenge to first-line proposals to accept residual risk

inferred_jobs.description: Challenged the vulnerability-flag coverage assumption and refused the delivery team's position that 61% coverage is representative.
Granted risk acceptance subject to a coverage improvement plan and a 90-day review.
Consumes a pack substantially duplicating the design authority's, prepared separately and cut at a different date.

decision_classes: Refusal escalating to Board Risk Committee
payload.challenge_role: Second-line challenge with refusal power. Evidenced working: a first-line position was rejected and a condition imposed.
escalation_out: Board Risk Committee — where the Forum refuses
payload.cadence: per change, seven days after the design authority
manual_reconstruction_steps: Risk pack prepared separately from the design authority pack despite substantially shared content
judgement_steps: Whether 61% vulnerability-flag coverage supports the cohort performance claim
independence_requirements: Refusal power must survive the accepting function's disagreement
Escalation to Board Risk Committee must remain available
Challenge must not be merged into the authority it challenges
contradictions: Four members shared with the design authority it is expected to challenge independently

veto_waiver_or_override_authority.holder: Risk Acceptance Forum — refusal, escalating to Board Risk Committee

accountability_terminus.holder: unresolved — 'the Chief Risk Officer's delegate', unnamed

independence_assessment.reporting: Chaired by the Chief Risk Officer's delegate — second line, not through the accepting function.
independence_assessment.authority: Refusal power escalating to Board Risk Committee. The strongest single indicator here.
independence_assessment.evidence_source: The pack is prepared by the Ashcombe delivery team. The Forum sees what the first line assembled.
independence_assessment.orchestration: Scheduled seven days after the design authority, on the delivery cycle.
independence_assessment.suppression_or_configuration_control: Not established. No source addresses whether the accepting function can scope or defer the Forum.
independence_assessment.cognition_or_model_source: Not applicable — the Forum's challenge is human and drew on evidence outside the pack's framing.

required_authority: Any change to the Forum's refusal power or its escalation route requires the authority that established raf-tor-v3. No source in the estate establishes who holds it.
caveat: Partial independence is a finding about seven dimensions, not a score. The refusal power is real and evidenced; the evidence source and the shared membership qualify it.
prohibited_inference: That overlapping packs make the Forum's purpose duplicative of the design authority's
That four shared members support consolidation — they weaken independence, not the case for merging
That efficiency in pack preparation is a reason to change what the Forum does
